outcome: LAUNCHED AND FAILED BEFORE SCIENCE, after materializing all five arms at their recorded identities, PASSING the generation-protocol attestation, and training the first probe. The per-probe generation admission then refused that probe: its rollouts were not produced under the attested protocol. No probe was scored; no ranking and no selection exist.
classification: ORDINARY ENGINEERING FAILURE, before formal measurement. The refusal is the fail-closed gate working: it detected that the generations carried a different runtime identity than the attestation, and stopped before a scorer could produce a number under an identity its evidence did not support. Nothing scientific was measured, so there is nothing to have retried or pooled. P12.1's pre-science clause applies: preserve and close this subrun, diagnose, repair, build a fresh chain under a new attempt identity.

root_cause.attested: f0db1b430df37c766e9117ac24c0cbd1a4c89420, observed by the engine probe, which received the pod image digest on its command line (--image-digest) and recorded runpod/pytorch:1.1.0-cu1300-torch291-ubuntu2404@580.126.09
root_cause.observed: a different digest, because `uncapped_eval.py` resolves the image digest from os.environ['AADISTILL_IMAGE_DIGEST'] ONLY -- it takes no --image-digest flag -- and the driver spawned it with a bare inherited environment that never carried that variable. The evaluator therefore recorded a null image digest and hashed a different runtime.
root_cause.why_it_was_invisible_until_now: the driver sets its own sys.path in process, which puts nothing in os.environ. Every subprocess it spawns inherits an environment the launcher populated for the DRIVER, not for the driver's children. The launcher does pass the digest on the driver's command line, and the driver did forward it to the engine probe as a flag -- so the attesting side had it and the evaluating side could not.
root_cause._this_is_the_same_shape_as_attempt_3: attempt 3 died because a pod-spawned subprocess could not resolve its own imports, for the same structural reason: a driver's in-process setup does not reach its children. That failure produced tests/integration/test_pod_script_imports_resolve.py, whose docstring states the contract explicitly -- 'a driver sets its own sys.path in process and that does NOT put anything in os.environ, so every subprocess it spawns inherits an environment with no PYTHONPATH'. The environment half of that same sentence was left unguarded.

repair.fix: scripts/stages/stage-1/phase_d1/autoinit_d1_behavioural_driver.py :: child_env(image_digest), wired into all four subprocess.run call sites (engine probe, trainer, evaluator, scorer). It copies os.environ and adds AADISTILL_IMAGE_DIGEST when the launcher supplied one, so every child observes the runtime the attestation describes.
repair.audited: every environment variable the driver's five spawned processes read. AADISTILL_IMAGE_DIGEST is the only one; both scorers read none. The fix is therefore complete for this class rather than a patch of the one observed site.
regressions: TestEverySubprocessGetsTheLauncherSuppliedEnvironment -- 5 tests: every subprocess.run in the driver passes env=child_env(...); the digest is carried; PATH survives; the key is omitted rather than set to 'None' when the launcher supplied nothing.
